newsitem.title: UK: LatAm Eurobonds in good shape despite YPF delay.
newsitem.headline: LatAm Eurobonds in good shape despite YPF delay.

text.p: LONDON, Nov 13 Reuter - Latin American Eurobonds were in good shape despite the recent hold-up of a major oil company's bond issue, analysts said.
Argentine oil and gas company YPF SA surprised the markets last week when it pulled a proposed five-year $200 million Yankee bond, postponing it until sometime in 1997.
"The fact that YPF has pulled is not any significant trend or turning point of the (international bond) market," a syndicate manager at a European bank told Reuters on Wednesday.
"The market is in very good shape. Spreads have been tightening and the markets should continue to grow for the rest of the year," he said.
"Following the downturn six weeks ago the market has more or less recovered," he said, adding Argentina's bonds had tightened 10 to 15 basis points in the last two weeks.
The YPF offering was delayed because a slightly weaker market did not allow it to meet aggressive funding targets, dealers said.
"When the market went down YPF realised they couldn't get the specific price and they were not desperate for the money so they decided to put (the bond issue) on hold," the trader said.
Analysts said they expected Latin American Eurobond markets to remain calm toward the end of year, as investors who have enjoyed a "wonderful year" took profits.
"Investors have had a pretty good year this year...and I don't see any further massive spread tightening before the year-end," an emerging market debt trader said.

Spreads on Latin American debt widened in October on the back of a weaker Mexican peso, triggering fears of a repeat of another devaluation crisis, and concerns about continued political turmoil inside some countries, especially Argentina.
This was still a factor, some traders said.

"I think people have been a bit concerned about Argentina for a few months given that it needs to borrow an awful lot, given that the government is trying to get difficult union reform through," the emerging market debt trader said.

Argentina's largest union confederation, the Confederacion General del Trabajo, on Tuesday got the go-ahead to organise a stoppage in January to protest proposed labour reforms, a union federation spokesman said.
It held a 24-hour general strike in August and a 36-hour stoppage in September.

The trader said this might affect the bond spreads in the next few months. "I certainly don't think it's a great buying opportunity right now but nor do I think it's a particular moment to sell," he said.
Analysts said they did not expect much volatility in the markets at the end of the year.
"People are very doubtful that the U.S. Treasury market is going to get much higher," the trader said.
"There's probably space for Brazil to tighten in slightly but the rest (LatAM paper) I think would just continue at the same spreads at the moment," the syndicate manager said.
